messages:
alex_reed: Quick heads-up — saw a 20-60ms tail latency bump on TP all-reduce when per-GPU msgsize hits ~110-140KB. Looks like kernel selector is toggling between tree and ring and we get serialization. :thinking:

maria_k: Can you paste the perf snippet? is this stable across runs?

alex_reed: Repro is pretty stable on the 8-GPU A100 rig. Small run log: 
```
./run_tp_synth.sh --micro-batch 1 --seq 1024 --msgsize-sweep 64k-256k
N=8, msg=120KB -> allreduce latency 34.2ms (tree) / 112.8ms (ring) observed intermittently
nvprof: kernel switch at iter 42 -> falling back to fallback_ring_path
```

sasha: Interesting. Did kernel selector log the heuristics? Maybe sequence length distribution pushed kernel costs over threshold and batching heuristics changed.

alex_reed: I dumped selector logs. snippet: 
```
[selector] chosen_kernel=tree heur=kv_frag_threshold=0.12 batch_score=0.78
[selector] switch -> ring because: predicted_kernel_cost_diff < 0 and nvlink_saturation=0.94
```

ray: NVLink saturation high + msgsize in that middle region can make ring slower due to extra steps. Are we seeing any KV cache flushes coincidentally? cache misses could increase in-flight windows and trigger different packing.

alex_reed: Good call — KV cache stats show sporadic flushes right before the jump. kvcache: prefix_hits=0.86, prefix_misses spike to 0.02 then flushes. Possibly batcher aligning different tensor boundaries.

maria_k: Could be our packer rounding that produces slightly larger messages after coalescing. Batcher heuristics: we currently use ``max_packet_bytes``=131072 and align to 128B. If coalesce pushes from 110KB -> 128KB it's near the threshold.

sasha: Actionable: add a temporary guard in kernel selector to prefer tree for 96KB-160KB until we instrument bandwidth curves more. That should avoid fallback oscillation. :+1:

ray: Also request bench-bot to do controlled sweep with forced tree and forced ring to gather steady-state numbers. @bench-bot can you run: 
```
bench-bot: run sweep --nodes 8 --msgsizes 64k,96k,128k,160k,192k --modes forced_tree,forced_ring,auto --out /tmp/tp_allreduce_sweep.json
```

bench-bot: scheduled run starting in 2m. Will post results when done. :robot_face:

alex_reed: For the repro steps I'm adding a tiny harness in `tools/tp_repro.py` to log nvprof + selector reasoning per-iter. Putting it on my branch now.

maria_k: When you have the data, let's plot comm/compute overlap and per-iter kernel choice. If overlap drops significantly when ring chosen we have a strong signal.

sasha: Also add a single-run flamegraph for the NCCL phases (send/recv/reduce) — ring tends to amplify tail if one hop lags.

ray: Long term: we should revise batcher alignment to avoid pushing into pathological msgsize bins. Maybe use adaptive rounding to keep coalesced msgs in stable buckets.

alex_reed: Agreed. Short term: guard in selector + bench sweep. I'll open PR to force-threshold and add telemetry flags to console for "kernel-oscillation" counter.

bench-bot: finished run: results uploaded -> /artifacts/tp_allreduce_sweep_318500.log

alex_reed: Initial numbers (from log): 
- 64k: tree 18.4ms / ring 21.0ms / auto picks tree
- 96k: tree 22.1ms / ring 45.8ms / auto picks ring sometimes -> 2x tail
- 128k: tree 28.9ms / ring 110.2ms / auto oscillates
- 160k: tree 35.0ms / ring 95.5ms / auto picks tree more often

maria_k: Clear sweet spots / cliffs. This is classic binning issue. Good catch.

sasha: I'll follow up with a small PR to selector to add hysteresis: require 5 iters of confidence before switching kernel. That should damp oscillations.

ray: + also expose the cache flush metric in runtime console so we can correlate in-prod.

alex_reed: I'll file a perf ticket with candidate mitigations: (1) selector hysteresis, (2) bucket-aware coalescing, (3) short-term forced-tree for 96-160KB, (4) telemetry for kernel-oscillation.

maria_k: Assign to alex_reed + sasha. I'll review PRs. Thanks team. :rocket:

sasha: tagging this for postmortem if it hits prod SLA.

alex_reed: Will push the forced-tree PR in ~30m and run full CI.

ray: Nice work. Keep an eye on any regression for very small msgs after change.

maria_k: noted.

alex_reed: End of thread — will update when PR merges.
